items.title: How propagandists weaponize archaeology to rewrite the past
items.description:
The historian Eric Hobsbawm once said, “Historians are to nationalism what poppy-growers … are to heroin-addicts. [They] supply the essential raw material.” The same holds true for archaeologists. The heritage archaeologists reveal helps groups of people forge collective identities and anchor our fleeting lives in something enduring. Spectacular discoveries — King Tut’s mask, the bronzes of Benin, Irish harps — also become national icons and rallying points.

items.title: Ease productivity overload with “niksen,” the Dutch art of doing nothing
items.description:
When was the last time you did nothing? By that, I don’t mean scrolling through social media, mowing the lawn, or fretting over the latest office drama. I mean a do-nothingness with no purpose and no goal other than to just enjoy being.

items.title: The universe built its own telescope out of space and time
items.description:
When you see the sun, you’re seeing it as it was eight minutes ago. When you see the Andromeda galaxy, the light reaching your eyes left 2.5 million years ago. Astronomer Michelle Thaller, who spent 28 years at NASA, explains why everyone who looks at the sky is looking back in time. She also explains how today’s telescopes can now see the universe as it was more than 12 billion years ago. 
 This video  The universe built its own telescope out of space and time  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: Why neutrality is worth chasing, even if no one gets there
items.description: Critics say neutrality is impossible, but Jimmy Wales, founder of Wikipedia and author of  The Seven Rules of Trust , argues that this is no reason to stop trying. In this conversation with Jonny Thomson, he explains why a fight over a single word, from “Gdańsk” to “security fence,” is often what an encyclopedia should explain. items.title: “One of the most stupid ideas” – a physicist on simulation theory
items.description:
Carlo Rovelli thinks the search for an “ultimate reality” is a mistake, and that physics, Buddhist philosophy, and Wittgenstein all point the same way. Jonny Thomson asks him what’s left once you give up on foundations. 
 This video  “One of the most stupid ideas” – a physicist on simulation theory  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The invention that changed reading forever (and it wasn’t the Kindle)
items.description:
We live in a time of technological revolution. The past 50 years have birthed the personal computer, the smartphone, and now artificial intelligence. While each is a world-changing invention and still relatively young, none yet rivals the movable-type printing press.

items.description:

items.title: Ask Ethan: What does it mean for atoms to “touch” each other?
items.description: One of the most counterintuitive things about existence is the notion of forces. In order to experience a force — that is, for one object to feel the influence of another object on it — two objects don’t necessarily even need to touch, or be in contact, with one another. items.title: Voyager’s cosmic map of Earth’s location: Cute, but wrong
items.description: Here in late 2026, an incredible milestone has been reached: the Voyager 1 spacecraft — humanity’s most distant spacecraft from Earth — has  finally passed a distance of one light-day  from us. Along with its twin, Voyager 2, these two spacecraft have left the confines of the Solar System and now traverse interstellar space, freely floating through the interstellar medium.
